create.name: Alan Finger
create.bio:
Alan Finger is the founder of ISHTA Yoga and has taught yoga and meditation for more than sixty years. He started practising at fifteen under his father, Mani Finger, and with several of the twentieth century's well-known swamis, and together father and son shaped the ISHTA approach. The letters of the name point to hatha, tantra and ayurveda brought together as one science, and the style joins breath-led flowing practice with alignment, meditation and bodywork. He carries the title Kavi Yogiraj and is regarded within ISHTA as a teacher of Kriya and Tantra.

Before ISHTA had its own home he helped found the studios Yoga Zone, Be Yoga and Yoga Works. Today he co-owns ISHTA Yoga's studio near Union Square in New York City with Mona Anand and his wife, Sarah Platt-Finger, gives signature lectures in its 200- and 300-hour teacher trainings, and helps lead an advanced course on the koshas for senior graduates. With Sarah he also hosts small retreats at their home in Delray Beach, Florida, built around dinacharya, the daily rituals of a committed practitioner, and ISHTA Diksha, the school's core meditation. His books include Chakra Yoga, written with Katrina Repka.

books.title: Chakra Yoga
books.author: Alan Finger and Katrina Repka
books.description: A short guide to the seven chakras from the ISHTA tradition, written with Katrina Repka. It explains each energy centre in turn and gives yoga practices for working with it.

courses.title: ISHTA Dinacharya Retreat with Alan and Sarah Finger
courses.description: A small five-day retreat at the Fingers' home in Delray Beach on the daily routines of a committed yogi and an updated form of ISHTA Diksha meditation. Days mix asana and meditation classes, talks and discussion, with Ayurvedic lunches.

courses.title: ISHTA Masters Program: Yoga through the Lens of the Koshas
courses.description: An advanced five-day hybrid course for graduates of ISHTA's 500-hour training, taught by its senior trainers including Alan Finger. Each day takes one of the five sheaths of the self through practice, talks and discussion.
